expect.note: every name this observation advertises for a combobox is a name resolve() accepts, fed back verbatim

provenance: T-M42-20 case (a) — the root cause of M42's unmet headline clause, and the only case in the suite that closes the observe->resolve loop instead of grading each end separately. `observe()` and `resolve()` compute the accessible name with two different engines: Chromium's `accessibility.snapshot()` applies the page's CSS `text-transform`, Playwright's locator engine does not. The inspector's picker is labelled `<label for="fx">select a committed fixture</label>` under a `.mode label{text-transform:uppercase}` rule, so the observation hands the planner `SELECT A COMMITTED FIXTURE` and `resolver.py`'s role tier — `get_by_role(role, name=name, exact=True)`, case-sensitive whole-string — cannot match it. `resolver.py`'s own comment, "planner names come from the observation verbatim", is exactly the assumption this breaks. Measured live at $0 on 2026-08-26 against https://whaleforce-sec10k.zeabur.app with 43 `<option>`s in the DOM, so it is not the empty-at-load race the block guessed at second (that half is case `action-select-option-waits-for-fetch-painted-options`); the committed snapshot `src/browser/fixtures/sec10k-inspector.html` reproduces it offline, byte for byte the same name. The case asserts the ROUND TRIP, not the uppercase string: pinning `SELECT A COMMITTED FIXTURE` in `contains` would have made the case red for the other legitimate fix (folding the case inside `observe`), and the invariant that matters is that the two ends agree, whichever end moves.

triage.red_first: observed as `{'role': 'combobox', 'name': 'SELECT A COMMITTED FIXTURE'}`; fed back, `resolve` raised `ResolveError: no tier resolved {'role': 'combobox', 'name': 'SELECT A COMMITTED FIXTURE'}`. Case output: `advertised_name_did_not_resolve: [{'target': {'role': 'combobox', 'name': 'SELECT A COMMITTED FIXTURE'}, 'error': "ResolveError: no tier resolved {'role': 'combobox', 'name': 'SELECT A COMMITTED FIXTURE'}"}]`. The same target lowercased resolved at tier `role`.
triage.note: 213 offline cases were green over this. The gap was structural: `observe` cases graded what the observation says and resolver cases graded targets an author typed, so no case ever handed one end's output to the other.
